goal: Give every effective v5 concept one concise learner-relevant English meaning instead of a pile of dictionary senses.
principles: Teach one intended everyday sense per stable concept ID.
Do not use slash-separated synonym piles.
For a straightforward synonym pile, keep the first learner-relevant sense and defer materially different senses to another concept ID.
Use an explicit override when the first slash item is incomplete, misleading, less useful, or conflicts with the concept ID.
Use a short parenthetical only when it disambiguates the intended sense.
Conversation chunks may use a natural full English utterance rather than a dictionary label.
Formal and reading-news cards should still use one clear recognition meaning.
